data.narrative:
Dawn Aerospace, a Series B space and aerospace company that has raised $25M to date, was valued using two applicable triangulation methods against a comp universe of 5 public tickers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including Cowboy Space Corporation, Aalyria, and SpaceX.

The stage-progression method applied a 1.9x step-up multiplier to the $25M total raised, yielding an implied valuation of $48M. The peer-median approach, anchored to four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables (Sierra Space at $8.0B, Cowboy Space at $2.0B, Aalyria at $1.3B, and Skyryse at $1.1B), produced a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range of $1.1B to $8.0B. Public-comp anchoring was not applicable due to the absence of target revenue disclosure, though the Space & Aerospace sector median trades at 27.4x P/S across public comparables.

The two-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $40M to $1.9B, with a median of $849M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around whether Stage-Progression (which treats raised capital as a floor proxy) or Peer-Median (which weights market comparables) better captures early-stage aerospace risk and upside. Near-term revenue traction and technology validation would be critical to narrowing this range.
